Combat-medic-standard trauma kits and training, built for the farm.

Farm Focused Trauma Care pairs an agriculturally-focused trauma kit with hands-on, mobile training — so the people who feed us aren't defenseless in the minutes before help arrives.

Get Involved See the FFAK Kit
The Problem

Agriculture is one of the most dangerous jobs in America — and help is often 20 to 60 minutes away.

The standard first-aid kit in most farm shops is built for splinters, not for what an auger, a PTO shaft, or a 1,200-lb animal actually does to a person. Most farm and ranch workers have never been trained in hemorrhage control, airway management, or shock recognition.

18.6 / 100k
Agricultural fatal injury rate — nearly 5× the all-industry average of 3.7/100k FTE
28–41
Farm-related deaths per year in Wisconsin alone, 2017–2023
~50%
Of fatal agricultural injuries hit workers age 55 and older
~29%
Of documented agricultural injuries are caused by falls
Sources: CDC/NIOSH Agricultural Safety and Health surveillance; U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Census of Fatal Occupational Injuries; Wisconsin farm-fatality reporting, 2025–2026. Figures should be re-verified before public/funder use.
The Solution

Two integrated products, one mission.

As a nonprofit, FFTC prices both to reach the farmhand and the smallholder — not just operations that can already afford private safety consulting.

KIT

The Farm First Aid Kit (FFAK)

An individual and site-level trauma kit designed around agricultural mechanisms of injury — amputation and crush injuries, large-animal trauma, falls, and severe bleeding far from definitive care. Offered in three tiers: Personal, Site, and Commercial/Ranch.

TRN

Mobile Trauma Training

Hands-on training delivered on-site — at the farm, the co-op, the county fair — via a mobile training unit, rather than requiring farmers to travel to a fixed classroom. Four course tiers, from a 2-hour Fundamentals course to a full Train-the-Trainer certification.

Evidence Base

Built on the same standards that train combat medics and trauma surgeons.

FFTC doesn't invent its own trauma doctrine — every technique traces back to a recognized, evidence-based framework, translated into plain-language instruction for a lay rural audience.

TCCC

Tactical Combat Casualty Care

The MARCH algorithm (Massive hemorrhage, Airway, Respiration, Circulation, Hypothermia) is the backbone of FFTC's field-response sequence.

ATLS

Advanced Trauma Life Support

Keeps FFTC's field-level teaching consistent with what the receiving trauma team expects.

BLS

Basic Life Support

CPR, AED use, and choking response — the foundational layer beneath every course tier.

ABLS

Advanced Burn Life Support

Burn assessment and management for grain dryer, fuel, electrical, and chemical exposure.

Plus international prehospital sources — including Tactical Emergency Casualty Care (TECC) and Stop the Bleed — so FFTC's approach stays current as prehospital trauma science evolves.

The FFAK: purpose-built for the farm, not a relabeled first-aid kit.

Every item traces back to a recognized trauma-care standard and a specific agricultural mechanism of injury — augers, PTO shafts, large-animal trauma, falls, and grain entrapment.

FFAK-Personal

Belt / truck kit, individual worker
  • CAT-style tourniquet
  • Compressed hemostatic gauze
  • Pressure/Israeli bandage
  • Vented chest seal
  • Laminated MARCH quick-reference card

FFAK-Site

Shop, barn, or cab kit — family operation
  • 2× tourniquets, 2× hemostatic gauze
  • Burn dressing + SAM splint
  • Airway adjunct
  • Expanded MARCH action card
  • Rigid, weatherproof case

FFAK-Commercial/Ranch

Crews & ranch vehicles, larger operations
  • 4× tourniquets, extended hemostatic supply
  • Large-animal trauma guidance card
  • Spinal-precaution kit
  • Triage tags (multi-casualty)
  • ATV / truck-bed mountable case
Every graduate of an FFTC Fundamentals or Advanced course takes home a free FFAK-Personal kit — training and equipment are delivered together, not sold separately.
Wisconsin · Iowa County Pilot

A flagship pilot with a built-in clinical partner.

FFTC's flagship pilot county is Iowa County, in Wisconsin's Driftless Area — a dairy- and livestock-heavy rural county served by Upland Hills Health, whose hospital is in Dodgeville with clinics reaching across the county:

  • Dodgeville (hospital + clinic)
  • Mineral Point
  • Highland
  • Montfort
  • Spring Green
  • Barneveld
  • Mt Horeb

FFTC's Founder serves as Chief Medical Officer of Upland Hills Health — giving the pilot a clinical leader and Medical Director from day one, and a seven-site network that doubles as a natural outreach and kit-distribution footprint as the program scales.

$203.7M

Wisconsin's year-one award from the federal Rural Health Transformation Program — part of a $50B, 5-year national initiative (2026–2031) aimed at rural care gaps like this one. FFTC's Iowa County health-system relationship is a direct, warm path toward a future Care Coordination partnership application, governed by a formal conflict-of-interest process.

Roadmap

Prove it in Wisconsin, then expand across the Upper Midwest.

Months 1–6

Incorporate in WI, recruit board, hire 2 founding staff, finalize kit design, confirm Iowa County + 1–2 more pilot counties.

Months 7–12

Build mobile unit, buy training equipment, produce pilot kits, deliver first Fundamentals/Advanced courses, launch Train-the-Trainer.

Year 2

Expand to 8–12 WI counties; pursue UW–Madison land-grant partnership and RHTP coordinated-care track.

Year 3

Scale to 20+ WI counties; first expansion county/region outside Wisconsin.
